issue.title: Launch admission cancellation summaries omit a launch error after preserving earlier launches
issue.description:
## CI failure

- **Node:** `tests/test_launch_admission_dispatch_core.py::test_cancel_open_units_does_not_erase_launched`

The companion `tests/test_launch_admission_mixed_matrix.py::test_cancel_after_first_mixed_unit_preserves_launched` fails the same way. Both preserve one launched unit but report `launch_errors=0` instead of `1`. Observed at HEAD `fc0abbd54c286f1dcf285bf1f717418ce9e3257b`; both failed in the broad check and in a serial rerun.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Both launch-admission cancellation tests failed in the broad check and reproduced serially on the unchanged tree, with launch_errors=0 where the tests expect 1.

issue.creation_reason: The required check reported two launch-admission cancellation tests failing, and both reproduced serially on the same tree. These failures are outside the video-preview files and need independent follow-up.

evidence.note: Independent observation during sase-1t3.10.1 landing: check ToolRun 6b3ba7450a20b7f13a341f55e64a1f40 failed the two launch-admission cancellation nodes; both reproduced serially on unchanged primary fbc1e34fbc with linked core 98a22b79. Causal diagnosis: Rust 98a22b79 deliberately makes Cancelled contribute skipped instead of launch_errors. Fresh origin review found companion primary commit 4e5c1b9730 already updates these exact assertions to skipped=1/launch_errors=0/outcome=cancelled and pins core 98a22b79. This report corroborates the older-primary/newer-core mismatch, not a reason to restore obsolete launch-error semantics; recheck on the paired revisions before changing behavior.

payload.description: Need duplicate reports and resolution context for four deterministic cancellation failures

This supports the existing older-primary/newer-core diagnosis; no new task or fresh failure corroboration is warranted.
